contracts.reason: Explicitly excluded from the frontend; no backend compatibility endpoint exists.
The implemented API consistently uses singular /api/chat.
Chat exposes runs and paused runs, but no chat state route.
All three implemented agent tools use /continue.

The Code surface renders it (2026-09-21): RecoveryPanel, mounted in the main region when the selected task's run is interrupted, showing the bounded step tail with totals over all of it, the leftover checkout with what a discard would lose, and a two-step discard that mirrors the backend's own force rule. Still partial for two reasons, both named in the panel rather than hidden behind a disabled control: resuming is a **re-run** (`POST /api/{tool}/run-task` with the same task id), which no surface can start yet, so the verb is reported with its reason and the route named instead of being actioned; and Cowork and Design have no surface of their own yet, so the panel is shared (`components/RecoveryPanel`) but only Code mounts it.
Served by the queue rather than a separate /api/attention/approvals path: approvals arrive as items with kind approval_required, carrying the tool, task and the call that answers them.

Served by the queue rather than a separate /api/attention/interrupted path: interrupted runs arrive as items with kind interrupted. The TaskRun contract carries the state too since migration 020 (boot reconciliation writes interrupted, not error), so an interruption is discoverable in both places it is read.

Enforced, not reported: 1.36 classifies every provider failure and applies a cooldown per class (401/403 60m, 402 30m, 429 5m or Retry-After, 404 2m, 5xx 1m, network 30s), and the router skips a cooled provider — but no read route says which provider is cooling or until when. The provider list is where that belongs, and nothing renders it yet.
The frontend has no provider-creation form: `POST /api/providers` is not called. `providerTypeSchema` accepts `puter` (1.38), so the type itself is no longer the gap — a settings screen is.

Nothing renders it yet. The route exists (1.38) and carries the credential kind, the catalogue URL, `requiresPaidPlan` and the note, so a settings form can warn before a token is pasted rather than after the first 402.
Code tasks can be listed globally; Cowork and Design have no task list.
Health summary has providers, MCP and errors but no backup component.

The spec asked for lineage by artifact id (`GET /api/artifacts/:id/versions`); the implementation serves it by artifact key (`GET /api/artifacts/versions?key=`, 1.39 A6), which is what the provenance panel calls. An id-based route would be a second way to ask the same question — artifact ids name a single version, while the lineage is the version list of one key.
Spending cap is part of the implemented limits contract.

The spec asked for `GET|PUT /api/settings/reload-config`; the implementation is a `POST`. A `PUT` would have to name what it replaces, and nothing is cached to replace — `db/settings.ts` keeps settings un-cached and project files are read per task — while the route itself only re-reads, validates and reports the on-disk configuration, which is why `docs/CONTRACTS.md` argues it adds no cache at all. The capability is present, so this row is a verb mismatch rather than a missing route: a client that followed the specification and sent a GET would get a 404.
The shell can federate list endpoints, but there is no global content-search contract.
